name: Linde

header.one_liner: Contracted industrial gases with pass-through pricing; steady, and priced like it.
header.thesis: Linde delivered a record $4.59 of adjusted EPS in Q3 and nudged full-year guidance up to $17.82 to $17.92 (8% to 9% growth). The shares have risen to about 29x that guide, while the sale-of-gas backlog slipped to $7.9B and engineering orders fell. The engine's base case still assumes a de-rating, so the expected return sits below the hurdle; the disagreement remains the exit multiple.

base.eps_label: FY2026 adjusted EPS, midpoint of updated guidance $17.82 to $17.92
base.rev_label: FY2026E sales ($B): nine months actual $27.47B plus a fourth quarter near Q3's $9.40B

rev_cagr.why: Q3 underlying sales rose 5% (3% price, 2% volume) and reported sales 9% with 1% currency. The Americas led at 9% underlying; EMEA managed 3%. The sale-of-gas backlog of $7.9B and $11B total project backlog support mid single digit growth, but the backlog is now shrinking, not growing.

margin_end.why: Adjusted net margin is about 22.4% on guided EPS. Q3 adjusted operating margin was 29.4%, 30 basis points lower than a year ago but flat excluding cost pass-through. The base case adds roughly twenty basis points a year from productivity and the $425M cost programme taken in Q3. This is the engine's judgment.
margin_end.source: Linde Q3 2026 release and 10-Q; engine judgment

share_chg.why: Linde bought back $2.63B of shares in the first nine months, about 1.5% of the market value annualised. The base case assumes about 1% a year net as capex of $5.5B to $6.0B absorbs more of the cash.
share_chg.source: Linde Q3 2026 10-Q (purchases of ordinary shares $2,632M, nine months)

exit_pe.why: Current multiple is about 29x guided 2026 EPS, up from 27.6x when this was last written, with the 10-year Treasury near 5.15%. The base case assumes a de-rating to 25x. This is the number that decides the stance.

pillars.title: Contracts lock in volume and pass through energy
pillars.claim: Most gas is sold under long contracts with minimum purchase terms and energy cost pass-through, so profit grows even when industrial volume is soft.

evidence.t: Q3 sales $9,404M, +9%; underlying +5% from 3% price and 2% volume
Americas underlying +9% (6% price, 3% volume); EMEA +3%; APAC +8%
EMEA margin down 80 bps reported but flat excluding cost pass-through

pillars.test: Does underlying sales growth stay at or above 3%?

pillars.title: Margin has stopped falling
pillars.claim: Adjusted operating margin of 29.4% was 30 basis points below last year, against a 60 basis point decline in Q2. Excluding pass-through it was flat, and the Americas expanded.

evidence.t: Americas 35.1% (+50 bps), EMEA 35.1% (-80 bps), APAC 27.4% (-70 bps)
$425M cost reduction and other charges: $200M severance, $42M other, $183M non-cash mainly US homecare

pillars.test: Does adjusted operating margin turn positive year on year in Q4?

pillars.title: Capital intensity is rising
pillars.claim: Nine-month capex was $4.17B and full-year capex is guided to $5.5B to $6.0B. Q3 free cash flow improved to $1,777M on $3,169M of operating cash flow.

evidence.t: Q3 capex $1,392M; free cash flow $1,777M; operating cash flow +8%

pillars.test: Does free cash flow cover dividends and buybacks in Q4?

pillars.title: The lead indicators cooled
pillars.claim: Engineering order intake fell to $499M from $871M in Q2, the third-party equipment backlog slipped to $2.9B, and the sale-of-gas backlog fell to $7.9B. Management says electronics proposal activity remains robust.

evidence.t: Engineering sales $582M, +12%; operating profit $107M, 18.4% margin; orders $499M

pillars.test: Do engineering orders recover above $800M a quarter, or does the gas backlog grow again?

variant.street: About 29x this year's guided earnings for the most defensive industrial: low volatility, contracted cash flows and an $11B project backlog.
variant.ours: The business case is intact and Q3 was a clean beat. The return case is weaker than before because the price rose while the backlog shrank; the engine needs a near-29x exit to reach the hurdle with Treasuries above 5%.
variant.could_be_wrong: If the backlog dip is plants starting up rather than fewer wins, and long rates fall, a 28x to 29x multiple is defensible and this becomes a positive stance.
variant.would_change_mind: Sale-of-gas backlog back above $8.0B with underlying volume above 3% for two quarters, or the price falling toward 22x guided EPS.

moat.summary: Local density, long contracts and pass-through pricing; Q3 margins held flat excluding pass-through in a soft industrial economy.
moat.detail: Existing Porter card (FY2025 10-K) rates Linde Strong.

quality.leverage_note: Total debt $26.7B against cash of $3.9B at 30 September 2026 (net about $22.8B, our arithmetic): modest against about $14B of annualised adjusted EBITDA (nine months $10.6B).
quality.incentive_note: Nine-month buybacks and dividends ($4.85B) exceeded free cash flow (about $3.5B); the gap is debt-funded.
checks: Reported EPS $3.66 (-11%) vs adjusted $4.59 (+9%): the gap is the $425M cost programme and Linde AG purchase accounting
$183M of the Q3 charge was non-cash and mainly in the US homecare business

catalysts.label: Linde Q4 2026 earnings and 2027 guidance (not yet announced; last year 5 February, some calendars show 11 February)
catalysts.note: Guide: Q4 adjusted EPS $4.40 to $4.50 (+5% to +7%). Last year Linde announced the date on 9 January.

tripwires.text: Q4 adjusted EPS below $4.40 (bottom of guide)

tripwires.note: Fell to $7.9B from $8.1B. The release does not split start-ups from new wins, so this may be conversion rather than weaker demand; the threshold is kept so the dispute stays visible.

risks: Industrial and chemical volume weakness in EMEA (underlying growth only 3% in Q3).
Electronics capex timing: the backlog and engineering orders both fell in Q3.

lenses.eisman: Adjusted EPS rose 9% while reported EPS fell 11%. Ask what the $425M programme and the homecare write-down say about the parts of Linde nobody talks about.
lenses.munger: A great business bought at 29x earnings is still an average investment if Treasuries pay more than 5%.
lenses.buffett: Exactly his kind of franchise; the price moved up while the backlog moved down, which is the wrong combination for a buyer.
lenses.hohn: Durable, contracted, pricing power: the cleanest profile of the four. The test is now whether the $7.9B backlog refills.

review.basis: Q3 2026 10-Q and release (quarter to 30 September 2026), with prices to the 13 November 2026 close; news reviewed to 16 November. Q4 and 2027 guidance come in early February; this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: The best operator in a three-player oligopoly, now at about 29x earnings. The business is not the debate; the premium is, and the backlog just stopped growing.
review.model: Linde sells industrial gases (oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, specialty gases) under long contracts, and builds the plants that make them.

how_it_earns.v: Plant built next to a customer, 15 to 20 year take-or-pay contract, energy costs passed through.
Liquid gas trucked locally. Density of plants and routes sets the cost advantage.
Cylinders to small users. Highest price per unit, most local.
Designs and builds plants for Linde and third parties. Lumpy, low margin, early signal of demand.

mix.note: Segment profit is Linde's own measure, excluding Linde AG merger purchase accounting. EBITDA adds back segment depreciation.

rows.label: Americas
rows.driver: Underlying +9%: 6% price, 3% volume from electronics, chemicals and energy, metals and mining

rows.label: APAC
rows.driver: Underlying +8% on 5% volume from new plants, electronics and chemicals

rows.label: Engineering
rows.driver: Project timing; $2.9B third-party backlog, $499M Q3 orders (Q2: $871M)

rows.label: Other
rows.driver: LAMT coatings and global helium wholesale

review.position: One of three global gas majors with Air Liquide and Air Products, and the largest by sales. Local density makes each regional market close to a duopoly.

sources: Switching cost of an on-site plant
moat.threat: Moat is safe. The return on new capital is what can slip.

what_numbers_say.d: Underlying sales +5% in Q3 (Q2: +4%): price +3%, volume +2%. The Americas carried it at +9%.
Adjusted operating margin 29.4%, down 30 bps (Q2: down 60 bps) and flat excluding pass-through. Americas margin rose 50 bps to 35.1%.

what_numbers_say.t: A charge sits under the beat
what_numbers_say.d: Adjusted EPS $4.59 (+9%), reported $3.66 (-11%). The $425M cost programme includes $200M severance and $183M non-cash, mainly US homecare.

what_numbers_say.t: Returns still exceed free cash flow
what_numbers_say.d: Nine months: buybacks $2.63B plus dividends $2.21B against about $3.5B of free cash flow (operating cash flow less $4.17B capex).

balance.read: Leverage is modest and the rating is protected, but shareholder returns are partly debt-funded.
facts: $2.09B of long-term borrowing in nine months, including €1.6B of notes issued in May
Management commits to strong Moody's and S&P ratings

flags.flag: Adjusted EPS excludes merger accounting and restructuring
flags.evidence: Q3 reported EPS $3.66 vs adjusted $4.59. The gap is the $425M cost reduction and other charges plus Linde AG purchase accounting, eight years after the merger.
$183M of non-cash Q3 charges relate primarily to the US homecare business. The 10-Q does not say whether more is to come.
Margin comparisons should use underlying sales; EMEA's 80 bps margin decline disappears excluding pass-through.

forecast_basis.rev_cagr: Driver-based: price plus volume plus backlog start-ups, cross-checked with guidance
forecast_basis.margin_end: Judgment: productivity and the Q3 cost programme offset inflation; Q3 shows margin flat ex pass-through
forecast_basis.share_chg: Below trend: buybacks ran about 1.5% a year; base assumes 1% as capex rises
forecast_basis.exit_pe: Judgment: de-rating from about 29x with 10-year yields above 5%

base.story: Price and start-ups carry 4% to 5% underlying growth, EPS compounds 8% to 9%, the multiple drifts lower.
base.needs: Pricing at or above inflation; the backlog refills as plants start up

downside.story: Industrial recession: volumes fall in EMEA and the Americas, price fades, the premium multiple compresses.
downside.needs: Underlying growth below 2% for two quarters

upside.story: Electronics fabs and clean-energy plants start up together; EPS growth reaches double digits and the multiple holds.
upside.needs: Backlog conversion plus volume recovery in EMEA

risks.how: Manufacturing and chemicals customers cut output, so merchant and packaged volumes fall. EMEA volume is already -1%.
Chip fabs are the main source of new on-site contracts. The sale-of-gas backlog fell to $7.9B and engineering orders to $499M in Q3.

risks.cause: Pricing power fades as inflation cools
risks.how: Linde's price gains track inflation. Price was +3% in Q3 and margin was flat ex pass-through; if price falls below cost inflation, margin compresses.

risks.cause: New capital earns less than old
risks.how: Capex is near 16% of sales. If new plants earn less than the 23.5% company return on capital, growth dilutes returns.
A 29x multiple competes with a 10-year Treasury yield above 5%. Higher-for-longer rates lower what investors pay for steady growth.

peer_read.why_premium: Linde earns more on capital than Air Liquide and Air Products, has a long record of beating its own guidance (Q3 EPS of $4.59 topped the $4.45 to $4.55 guide), and has avoided the large project write-downs that hit Air Products.
peer_read.why_not: Air Products' normalised EBITDA margin is higher, and Air Liquide trades at a lower multiple on similar consensus growth. The premium rests on execution, not structural superiority.
peer_read.peers_note: Air Liquide reports half-yearly, so its trailing figures are the last full fiscal year.

questions: Is the backlog dip plants starting up, or fewer electronics wins?
Should a $425M restructuring and eight-year-old merger accounting both sit outside adjusted EPS?
Is debt-funded buyback spending a sign of confidence or of a mature business?

review.title: Best in class, priced for it
review.lead: We rate Linde {rating} with a 12-month target of {pt} ({upside} upside, {ret} total return against a cost of equity of {hurdle}). Q3 was a clean beat and margins stopped falling, but the shares now trade at about 29x guided earnings while the backlog shrank, and our next-year EPS is {vs_cons} consensus.
review.call_reason: Quality is fully reflected: the target implies {ret} over 12 months against a cost of equity of {hurdle}.

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Underlying sales grew 5% in Q3, 3% from price and 2% from volume, led by the Americas at 9%. The sale-of-gas backlog slipped to $7.9B and engineering orders fell to $499M, so the next leg of growth is less visible than it was in Q2.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: Long take-or-pay contracts, local route density and energy pass-through make each regional market close to a duopoly. The moat is not the question; the return on the next dollar of capex is.

arguments.label: Profitability
arguments.text: Adjusted operating margin of 29.4% leads the sector and was flat excluding pass-through, an improvement on Q2. Reported EPS fell 11% on a $425M cost programme that management expects to lift productivity.

arguments.label: Capital
arguments.text: Buybacks and dividends of $4.85B in nine months ran ahead of free cash flow of about $3.5B, with the gap funded by debt, while capex rises to $5.5B to $6.0B for the year. Leverage is still modest.

arguments.label: Valuation
arguments.text: {peer_line} On our numbers the shares return {ret} over 12 months, short of the cost of equity.

thesis_long: Linde is the highest-quality way to own industrial gases. Contracts, density and pass-through pricing make its profit stream unusually predictable: Q3 adjusted EPS was a record $4.59, up 9%, and full-year guidance was raised to $17.82 to $17.92. We do not argue with any of that.

What we question is how much more the market will pay for it. The stock has risen to about 29x this year's guided earnings and trades at a premium to Air Liquide and Air Products on forward EV/EBITDA, while 10-year Treasuries yield above 5%. Meanwhile the lead indicators cooled: the sale-of-gas backlog fell to $7.9B, engineering orders nearly halved from Q2, and EMEA grew only 3%. A $425M restructuring, including a write-down in US homecare, sits outside adjusted EPS.

Our base case has EPS compounding about 7% a year with a de-rating to 25x, which leaves a 12-month return well short of the cost of equity. The upside case needs electronics start-ups to refill the backlog while long rates fall; the downside is an industrial recession that takes volume and the premium multiple together. We would turn more positive on a backlog back above $8.0B with volume growth above 3%, or a price nearer 22x earnings.

upside_risks.cause: The backlog refills with electronics wins
upside_risks.how: Management says proposal activity remains robust in electronics. New on-site contracts would lift the backlog back above $8B and support faster volume growth.
Lower Treasury yields would re-rate defensive compounders, and a 29x multiple would then look sustainable.
